reranked_evidence.snippet: # New Delhi Air Pollution Index Further Pushes for EV Adoption in India. India’s latest push toward electric vehicles is being driven by more than industrial policy or climate commitments. It is also a response to one of the country’s most persistent public‑health crises: air pollution. The Delhi government has approved a sweeping new electric‑vehicle policy that offers owners of older vehicles more than US$1,000 to scrap their cars and replace them with battery‑electric models. Delhi’s struggle with air pollution is well‑documented by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), India’s official air‑quality regulator. Through the National Clean Air Programme’s PRANA portal, the CPCB tracks air‑quality trends and the implementation of clean‑air action plans across more than 130 non‑attainment cities—urban areas that consistently fail to meet national standards. On its official website, the government describes the EV Policy as one of the world’s most progressive because its central objective is to “drastically reduce vehicular air pollution” while positioning Delhi as a global leader in EV adoption.
